title: Exploring techniques to assess stress-related physiological responses in captive African penguins☆
author: Currin, Ganswindt, et al.

steps.title: Lyophilize and pulverize feces
steps.instruction: Freeze‑dry the frozen urofaecal samples, pulverise the dried material into a fine powder and sieve through a wire‑mesh strainer to remove fibrous material.

steps.title: Weigh and extract with ethanol
steps.instruction: Transfer 0.050–0.055 g of the faecal powder into a tube, add 1.5 mL of 80 % ethanol, vortex for 15 min, then centrifuge at 1500 × g for 10 min.

steps.title: Collect supernatant and store
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant into labeled microtubes and store at –20 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Quantify ufGCM by EIA
steps.instruction: Run the tetrahydrocorticosterone enzyme immunoassay on the extracts as previously established; assay sensitivity 9.6 ng/g dry faecal mass, intra‑assay CV 3.36 % (high) and 4.38 % (low), inter‑assay CV 7.36 % (high) and 8.76 % (low); verify that serial dilutions give displacement curves parallel to the standard curve (slope variation < 5 %).

steps.title: Liquidise feather samples
steps.instruction: Process feather samples using the liquidisation method described in reference [36] to obtain a homogeneous extract.

steps.title: Centrifuge feather extracts
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the liquidised feather extracts for 10 min at 1500 × g to separate remaining solid material.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant and store
steps.instruction: Pipette the supernatant just below the surface into labeled microcentrifuge tubes and store at –20 °C until hormone analysis.

steps.title: Quantify corticosterone by EIA
steps.instruction: Run the corticosterone enzyme immunoassay on the feather extracts as per reference [37]; assay sensitivity 28 ng/g feather mass; note that parallelism was not assessed because a single dilution was used for all samples.
